findings.title: Billing target company differs from company authorizing admin permissions
findings.root_cause: The initial admin guard resolved permissions for cookie company A while companyId override B was approved only by active membership/lifecycle. Service-role/provider calls then operated on B.
findings.proof: Direct synthetic Node22 execution of actual guard, actual membership scope helper and actual dispute route: A billing.write + B viewer + body companyId B ->200; provider_dispute B and service UPDATE B reached. New actualguard+7route behavior suite RED15/24, GREEN24/24.
findings.impact: User with rights in one company could read or operate billing records and provider state of a different active-member company without the required billing permission there.
findings.fix: Optional explicit company on canonical admin guard, exact resolved target equality, and seven routes authorize target before effects. Default guard selection retained for other callers.
findings.false_positive_gates: Actual canonical resolver scopes role permissions; actual assertUserCanOperateCompany checks membership/lifecycle but no permission. Service client bypasses RLS. Provider client performs tenant credential selection, not actor RBAC. Explicit-B denied/authorized positive tests.

findings.title: Provider status GET bypasses canonical state transition and event-clock persistence
findings.root_cause: Remote getInvoice failure normalized null to unknown and replaced status_payload. Successful stale poll also unconditionally rewrote paid/credited state without providerEventProcessor transition or event-time guards.
findings.proof: Actualroute synthetic repro paid + stored last_provider_event_occurred_at -> provider outage ->200, unknown and clock erased. New tests RED3/3 failure, GREEN3/3 preserving paid/credit and event clock.
findings.impact: Invoice status could regress and lost event clock allows old later callbacks to evade stale-event prevention.
findings.fix: GET is diagnostic-only; successful observation DTO unchanged, no DB UPDATE. Invoice lookup rejection returns structured503 code invoice_provider_status_unavailable/trace_id and Retry-After60. Signed provider events remain canonical state writer.
findings.intentional_behavior_change: Internal status poll no longer persists observations. Admin documentation should describe diagnostics versus canonical stored settlement. No public contract change.

findings.title: Inbound automation accepts foreign message ID without binding operator company
findings.trigger: Authenticated operator with ediel.write in company A submits retained inbound message UUID of company B. UUID secrecy is not an ownership control.
findings.complete_chain: Selected-company admin check -> evaluator receives only messageId/forceManualReview -> service-role SELECT ediel_messages id only -> adopts message.company_id B -> tenant-B metering/customer authorization queries -> tenant-B decision/manualreview upserts -> returns Bcompany/customer/site/metering/Ediel identifier data. forceManualReviewtrue creates/reopens manualreview path.
findings.native_refutation: Coordinator supplemental actual catalog states all3baseRLS tables have service_role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE grants; decision/manualreview user trigger only guards history TRUNCATE; source message triggers validate canonical/environment/receipt/operationalcompany, none bind current session company for decisionwrite. RLS service-role does not restore operator tenant scope.
findings.live_effect_limit: No foreign message read/write, customer record value, or request executed. Conditional structurally exploitable boundary established from source/native metadata, not observed breach.
findings.targeted_fix: Operator route/evaluator must accept bound current company+actor, assert scoped permissions, query own message by company+id before any parsed data or writes; preserve service worker callers only with explicit authority. Root owns fix, this pass no sourcewrites.

post_remediation_source_recheck.review: Route rejects missing canonical guard.companyId, evaluator requires trustedcompany, initial service SELECT binds company_id+messageUUID before parsing/writes; foreignID yields404. Current corrected source checked; native tables/grants/trigger supplement proves original condition, not deployment of branch fix.
post_remediation_source_recheck.authority: Current source +native catalogue; no tests used asauthority and none run by this followup.

findings.title: Untouched billing/pricing and document routes resolve a second tenant after authorization
findings.trigger: No selected company cookie; active nonowner membership with role writer/read rights B is earliestcreated for canonical selection, and independently unordered service membership result starts with active viewer company A. Native guard grants B; second resolver chooses A.
findings.complete_chain: Native canonical resolver orders owner then membership.created_at and requires active user role; membership helper selects active memberships without order and chooses firstowner/firstrow, ignores user_role/is_active in same selection. Route action uses secondcompany instead of guardcompany. Docentityguard compares secondcompany, so foreignA object can pass despite authorizedpermissionsB.
findings.impact: Permission held for B can authorize read/write or document read in A under differing fallback order/eligible membership population. Company predicates remain present but bind the wrongly resolved company.
findings.refutations: Explicit valid cookie normally keeps both same; fixed7override routes now use canonical target/guardcompany. No existing badorder membership response/live request claimed.
findings.targeted_fix: One authoritative guardcompany, require nonnullcompany for company-specific route; entity guard compares guardcompany for tenantactor. Root owns bounded fixes; no sourcewrites in followup.

post_remediation_source_recheck.review: Sixbilling/pricingmethods now call requireAdminOperationalCompany(access.guard): nonplatform nullscope rejects; explicit canonicalcompany passed to existing lifecycle/membership guard rather than independent defaultselection. Entityguard compares requestedrecord company to guard.companyId before lifecyclecheck; canonical platform crosscompany semantics retained.

findings.title: Invoice dispute still overwrites the authoritative provider event clock
findings.trigger: Stored paid/provider event at12:00; successful manual dispute at13:00 overwrites status_payload={dispute:result}; later signed unpaid event occurred11:30 arrives.
findings.complete_chain: Dispute removes last_provider_event_occurred_at -> processor parse(lastclock)=null -> staleByTimefalse -> disputed allows unpaid in actual transitiontable -> CASstatecheck passes and older unpaid can persist. No fulltransaction test authority used.
findings.native_refutation: invoice_export_items service writes granted in native catalogue; no alternate surviving timestamp consulted by processor. Guardcompany fixed does not preserve eventclock. Native trigger/provider-call success outcomes conditional.
findings.impact: Delayed provider event can regress newer settlement/operator state after a legitimate dispute; history projection loses reconciliationtime.
findings.targeted_fix: Preserve authoritative status_payload metadata and apply safe operator transition/current-row fencing; root owns fix, no sourcewrites.

post_remediation_source_recheck.review: After successful providerdispute, source rereads latest current provider_status/status_payload/updated_at; preserves fullpayload+adds dispute snapshot; conditional UPDATE fences completeJSONB+updated_at, retriesmax5. Credited/cancelled preserved. Unknown local completion after providercommit returns truthful503/code. Actual source checked; no provider/race/native mutation executed.

source_boundary_review.snapshot_status: Final handler hash equals reviewed static callgraph snapshot; updated sharedguard/entityguard hashes are recorded separately.

source_boundary_review.authority: Actual route/function source and captured database catalogue; tests are availability metadata only and not correctness authority.

source_boundary_review.boundary_result: Boundary source reviewed; deeper business native/provider/storage effects remain explicitly unverified.

cron_review.auth: Fails closed without configured secret; Bearer/dedicated-header matching uses timingSafeEqual after equal-length check, or isAnalyticsCronAuthorized/authorizeScheduledRequest equivalent.
cron_review.actor_company: Cron credentials authorize privileged server automation rather than tenant public callers. Scope is server queue/company list or authenticated cron override.
cron_review.edge_notes: Static native-missing candidates under optionalCronStep, conditional queues, type branches or retry loops are not counted as mandatory broken methods. email/outbox/process writes blocked-run diagnostics before auth, but sender effects remain gated.

source_boundary_review.snapshot_status: Final handler hash equals reviewed static callgraph snapshot; updated sharedguard/entityguard hashes are recorded separately.

route_methods.tenant_ownership: Canonical authenticated tenant context plus required permissions; Ediel native functions additionally check grants/source authority. Entity guard where applicable.
route_methods.test_mapping_basis: Direct route or direct non-generic imported module reference; availability only, not executed coverage.
route_methods.rpc_trace_limit: Static string names in three import levels; candidate inventory, not full dynamic call graph/grant approval.

source_boundary_review.authority: Actual route/function source and captured database catalogue; tests are availability metadata only and not correctness authority.
